Retardmaxxing
ree-TARD-maks-ing
noun / verb (internet / Gen-Z slang)
From the "-maxxing" suffix family (looksmaxxing, mewing) meaning to maximize a trait, attached to a crude word for the cognitively impaired; current internet slang for deliberately embracing foolishness, low effort, or anti-intellectualism — often half-ironic.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

📖 Biblical Definition

Retardmaxxing is internet slang for deliberately leaning into foolishness: maximizing the appearance or practice of stupidity, taking the low-effort path on purpose, treating thoughtlessness as a flex. It belongs to the "-maxxing" family that began with looksmaxxing, and like much of that family it runs half-ironic — the user often knows better and is performing the bit. The dictionary decodes it on two levels. The surface level is the counsel of folly, and Scripture's whole wisdom literature stands against it: "how long, ye simple ones, will ye love simplicity?... fools hate knowledge" (Prov 1:22); the great commandment requires loving God "with all thy mind" (Mark 12:30); the believer is to be renewed in the spirit of his mind (Rom 12:2) and "in understanding be men" (1 Cor 14:20). To make a banner of deliberate stupidity is to despise a faculty God gave for His worship. The deeper level is the slur the word is built on: it makes sport of cognitive disability, and on that the LORD is not neutral — "thou shalt not curse the deaf, nor put a stumblingblock before the blind" (Lev 19:14). As with all such speech, the heart and the hearer decide the matter (see corrupt communication): the ironic shrug is not the same sin as real contempt, but a tongue trained to crown folly and mock the weak is being trained away from the mind of Christ.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

Internet slang (from the "-maxxing" family) for deliberately embracing foolishness or low effort, often half-ironic. Decoded against the call to love God with all the mind (Mark 12:30) and the guard over the weak (Lev 19:14). See corrupt communication for the heart-principle. Verdict: examine.

RETARDMAXXING, n./v. (internet / Gen-Z slang) Deliberately maximizing foolishness, low effort, or anti-intellectualism; treating thoughtlessness as a flex.

From the "-maxxing" suffix (looksmaxxing, mewing) = to maximize a trait, on a crude word for the cognitively impaired.

Frequently half-ironic — a performed bit rather than a sincere creed.

Surface decode: the counsel of folly, which Proverbs and the great commandment (love God with all thy mind) oppose.

Deeper decode: it trades on mocking disability — weighed by heart and hearer (see corrupt communication; Lev 19:14).

📖 Key Scripture

Mark 12:30 — "And thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind, and with all thy strength: this is the first commandment."

Prov 1:22 — "How long, ye simple ones, will ye love simplicity? and the scorners delight in their scorning, and fools hate knowledge?"

1 Cor 14:20 — "Brethren, be not children in understanding: howbeit in malice be ye children, but in understanding be men."

Rom 12:2 — "And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind, that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A counsel of folly with a slur for a root: it crowns deliberate stupidity (against the command to love God with the mind) and makes sport of cognitive disability (against the guard over the weak). The ironic user is not the contemptuous one — but the tongue is trained either way.

expand to see more

Folly as a flex. The age oscillates between idolizing the mind (see looksmaxxing's cousin, the optimization cult) and idolizing its abdication. Retardmaxxing is the second: weariness with effort dressed up as a lifestyle. But the mind is not a burden to be shed; it is a faculty given for worship — love the Lord with ALL thy mind (Mark 12:30) — and Proverbs treats the love of simplicity as a peril, not a vibe (Prov 1:22). To be renewed in Christ is to have the mind transformed (Rom 12:2), not anesthetized.

The root and the heart. The word is built on mockery of the cognitively impaired, and there the believer remembers whose image the impaired bear and Whose law guards them: curse not the deaf, nor trip the blind (Lev 19:14); mock not the poor, lest you reproach their Maker (Prov 17:5). Whether a given use is sin is, as always, decided by the heart and the hearer (see corrupt communication) — the self-deprecating shrug differs from real contempt. But a mouth trained to crown folly and laugh at weakness is drifting from the mind of Christ, and the wise will not make a home in that drift.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

The "-maxxing" suffix (maximize a trait) on a crude word for the cognitively impaired; internet slang for embracing deliberate foolishness — against loving God with all the mind (Mark 12:30) and the guard over the weak (Lev 19:14).
